chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Five prayers are not to be neglected in any state: when you perform Tawaf of the House, and when you intend to enter Ihram, and the Salat of the Eclipse, and when you forget [a prayer] so pray it when you remember, and the Salat of the Funeral.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five prayers that should never be neglected according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies five prayers that are universally obligatory or highly emphasized, ensuring they are never neglected regardless of one's state. These include the two-rak'ah prayer during Tawaf, the prayer preceding Ihram, the Eclipse prayer (Salat al-Kusuf), the makeup prayer for forgotten obligatory prayers, and the Funeral prayer. This highlights the structural consistency of Shia jurisprudence in linking ritual acts to specific moments of worship and transition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan and Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Five Salāts you cannot neglect upon every state – When you perform Tawaaf of the House (Kabah), and when you intend to wear the Ihraam, and Salāt of the eclipse, and when you forget so you pray when you remember, and Salāt of the funeral’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar all from Safwan ibn Yahya Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Five Salah (prayer) are not neglected in any condition. Such Salah (prayer) are after performing Tawaf, when you are about to have Ihram, for eclipse, to make up when remembering one forgotten and Salah (prayer) for a deceased.’”
